$comment: Gazetteer. coord = [lon, lat] WGS84. ALL coordinates are Phase-1 working values (coordVerified=false) and must be checked against GeoNames / Survey of India / satellite imagery before rendering. Precision tells the renderer how to draw: site=point, locality=small halo, regional=label only, unidentified=no point (text-only mention). Modern place names are used as anchors only where the historical site is at or near the modern town.

places.name: Mong Mao (Tai Mao heartland, Shweli valley)
places.notes: Anchored near modern Ruili/Shweli valley. The 13th-century political centre is not securely located. Do not draw a polygon.

places.name: Mong Mit / 'Maulung' (Sukaphaa's traditional homeland)
places.notes: Identification disputed in the literature. Render as text in narrator panel only.

places.name: Hukawng Valley
places.notes: Commonly proposed approach to the Patkai; the specific route is reconstructed, not documented.

places.name: Nong Nyang lake (Nawng Yang)
places.notes: Chronicle name; identification with the present Nawng Yang lake near the Pangsau Pass is conventional but should be marked approximate.

places.name: Namrup
places.notes: Also the refuge of Ahom kings during the Koch (1562-63) and Mughal (1662) occupations.

places.name: Tipam
places.notes: Area on the Burhi Dihing; exact early-13th-c. locality approximate.

places.name: Abhaypur
places.notes: Low confidence location.

places.name: Habung
places.notes: North-bank tract; settlement abandoned per chronicles due to floods. Low confidence location.

places.name: Charaideo
places.notes: First capital (1253 per chronicle chronology); later royal necropolis (moidams). Use UNESCO property coordinates once fetched.

places.name: Sadiya
places.notes: Associated with the Chutia kingdom and the post-1523 Ahom office of Sadiyakhowa Gohain. Chutia capital location(s) are debated; use Sadiya as an approximate anchor. River courses here have shifted substantially.

places.name: Garhgaon
places.notes: Capital from c. 1540; occupied by the Koch (1562-63) and by Mir Jumla (1662-63).

places.name: Rangpur (Sivasagar area)
places.notes: 18th-century capital (Rudra Singha onward). Not to be confused with Rangpur in present-day Bangladesh.

places.name: Jorhat
places.notes: Capital from 1794.

places.name: Dimapur (Kachari / Dimasa capital)
places.notes: Monolith ruins survive. Ahom sack dated 1536 in standard accounts.

places.name: Maibang
places.notes: Later Dimasa capital in the North Cachar hills.

places.name: Khaspur
places.notes: Later Kachari capital in the Cachar plains. Low confidence coordinate.

places.name: Kaliabor
places.notes: Seat of the Ahom western frontier command before Guwahati was secured.

places.name: Tezpur
places.notes: Modern orientation label only.

places.name: Guwahati
places.notes: Seat of the Mughal faujdar and later of the Ahom Borphukan.

places.name: Itakhuli fort
places.notes: Fortified hill at Guwahati; exact fort footprint to be verified.

places.name: Saraighat (Brahmaputra narrows at Guwahati)
places.notes: Battle zone along the river; render as a river reach, not a point.

places.name: Alaboi
places.notes: North-bank site near Guwahati (1669 battle). Location to be researched; show as text only until identified.

places.name: Barnadi river (mouth)
places.notes: North-bank boundary under the 1639 settlement.

places.name: Manas river (confluence with the Brahmaputra)
places.notes: Western Ahom limit after 1682 in standard accounts.

places.name: Dhaka (Jahangirnagar)
places.notes: Seat of the Mughal subahdar of Bengal in the 17th century (Mir Jumla's base). Source to add.

places.name: Sylhet
places.notes: Orientation label (Bengal).

places.name: Imphal (Manipur)
places.notes: Orientation anchor for the Manipur kingdom.

places.name: Naga Hills
places.notes: Region label only. Many independent communities; do NOT draw a polity.

places.name: Lushai Hills
places.notes: Region label only; outside Ahom political sphere in this period.

places.name: Ava (Inwa)
places.notes: Burmese royal capital; Amarapura was the capital c.1783-1823 - choose label by date.

places.name: Amarapura
places.notes: Konbaung capital during the 1817-1822 invasions (to verify).

places.name: Yandabo
places.notes: Village on the Irrawaddy where the treaty was signed. Coordinate low confidence.

polities.name: Ahom kingdom
altNames: Mong Dun Shun Kham (Tai name, verify)
